title: Opening and Withdrawing Coverage Review Cases under the Utilization Management Program
content:
The following terms govern how a coverage review case under the Utilization Management Program comes into existence and how it may be withdrawn.

**Who opens a case.** A case is opened by the prescriber or, when the package allows member-initiated review, by the member or an authorized representative, for one drug and one review type. The prescriber's clinical information is required to decide it whoever opens it.

**Urgency.** A case is urgent only on the prescriber's attestation while the package requires that attestation. A member's own statement of urgency does not make it urgent, and when the package allows a downgrade, a request filed as urgent without that attestation is handled as standard.

**Program status.** A case may be opened only while the member's review program is active.

**One undecided case per drug and review type.** While the package allows only one open case per drug and review type, only one undecided case may exist for the same member, drug and review type: a new case may be opened only when no case for the same drug and review type is still undecided.

**Withdrawal.** An undecided case may be withdrawn by its requester or the member when the package allows withdrawal; a withdrawn case is never decided.

## What is checked, and against what

| Condition | Evidence | Object it attaches to |
|---|---|---|
| Review program is active | the status of the member's review program in the system records | the review program the case is opened on |
| No undecided case for the same drug and review type | the member's case history: an opening with no approval, denial or withdrawal after it | same member, same drug, same review type |
| Case is still undecided (for withdrawal) | the case's history shows no approval, denial or withdrawal | the case being withdrawn |

## Combinations for a new case

| Review program | Undecided case already on file for the same drug and review type | New case may be opened |
|---|---|---|
| Active | No | Yes |
| Active | Yes | No |
| Pending effective or terminated | either | No |

### Hypothetical cases

- A member with an undecided prior authorization case for Humira asks to open a quantity limit exception case for Humira: the review types differ, so the open prior authorization case does not stand in the way.
- A member calls in distress and asks for an urgent review, but the prescriber has not attested: the member's statement does not make the case urgent, and on a package that allows the downgrade the request is handled as standard.
